steps.name: Hallmark preranked GSEA
caveats: A 12,000-gene background truncates hallmark sets - absent genes are not measured-and-unchanged, and NES is computed only over represented members; say so when reporting.

Hallmark sets overlap (several inflammatory sets share large gene blocks), so multiple significant inflammatory hallmarks are not independent findings - inspect leading-edge overlap before counting them separately.
GSEA on a 6 vs 6 ranking inherits that noise; a significant NES is a coordinated-shift claim, not a mechanistic one.
Do not read a hallmark NES as pathway activity in the causal sense - it is expression of set members, not signalling flux.
steps.context: The research question asks specifically for hallmark pathways, so hallmark is the required primary resource; GO BP is optional colour. Preranked GSEA over the full ranking is used rather than over-representation of a thresholded list because it uses the whole effect-size ordering and does not depend on an arbitrary cutoff - important at n=6 per group. The matrix carries 12,000 of ~20,000 human genes, so hallmark coverage is partial by construction.
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are coordinately up- or down-regulated in atopic-dermatitis lesional skin relative to control?
constraints: Use the shrunken-LFC ranking over ALL genes tested in T1S2's primary run - do not pre-filter to significant genes.
Match on HGNC gene symbol directly; the data is human, so no ortholog mapping and no ID conversion.
Report represented-set-size alongside nominal set size for every hallmark and drop sets with fewer than 10 represented members, stating how many were dropped.
Set and report a fixed random seed.
Report BH-adjusted p-values across the tested hallmark sets; significance at padj<0.05.
Cross-reference leading-edge genes of each significant hallmark to their DESeq2 LFC and padj so pathway calls are traceable to individual genes.
Hallmark is required for the primary result; any GO BP output must be clearly labelled exploratory.
Name the reference resource actually used in the output.
steps.description: Run preranked GSEA (fgsea multilevel) on the shrunken-LFC ranking of all tested genes from T1S2, against the human hallmark gene set collection - the 50 HALLMARK_* sets in HGNC symbols, resolved from the environment's reference store. The count matrix is already symbol-keyed, so join directly on gene symbol with no ID conversion. Report the fraction of each hallmark set's members present in the 12,000-gene ranking and exclude sets with fewer than 10 represented members. Report NES, pvalue, BH padj, nominal size, represented size and leading-edge genes for every set; call significance at padj<0.05. Produce a dot/bar plot of significant hallmarks ordered by NES and enrichment curves for the top 5 up and top 5 down. As secondary, exploratory annotation only, run the same preranked test against the human GO Biological Process collection if present, and use it solely to describe what the significant hallmarks are made of. If the hallmark resource cannot be resolved at run time, stop and report that - do not substitute another collection for the primary result.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea results for all hallmark sets surviving the representation filter, with NES, pval, padj, size, represented size and leading edge.
Per-set coverage against the 12,000-gene background reported and the number of dropped sets stated.
Significant hallmarks (padj<0.05) plotted by NES with direction unambiguous relative to lesional-vs-control.
Leading-edge genes cross-referenced to their DESeq2 statistics.
Any GO BP output explicitly marked secondary/exploratory.
The reference resource used is named.

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq count matrix from Salmon (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples; counts.csv) with a metadata table (metadata.csv, 12 x 2) encoding 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional skin samples vs 6 controls, unpaired. The question has two parts (which genes change, which hallmark pathways change) plus an explicit flag that sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median.

The shallow sample is handled first and explicitly (T1S1). A 4x depth deficit is not by itself grounds for exclusion: DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors absorb depth differences, and dropping 1 of 6 costs real power. But shallow libraries lose low-count genes and can behave as outliers in the dispersion fit. T1S1 quantifies the problem (library sizes, detected genes, size factors, VST PCA, sample-sample correlation, RLE/Cook's leverage) and decides on evidence whether sample_01 is merely shallow (keep) or a true outlier (flag). It does not delete the sample; it emits a keep/drop decision consumed downstream.

T1S2 runs the primary contrast - lesional vs control, ~condition, unpaired, single batch - with median-of-ratios normalisation, independent filtering, Wald test, BH FDR, and apeglm shrinkage for ranking. Because the depth imbalance is the one identified threat to validity, T1S2 runs the identical model twice, with and without sample_01, and reports concordance. If the gene list is stable the full-12 result is primary; if not, that instability is itself the finding.

T2S1 takes the shrunken-LFC ranking over all tested genes (not a thresholded list - preranked GSEA is the right test for 'which hallmark pathways change' at n=6 per group) and runs fgsea against the 50 human MSigDB hallmark sets, which are present in the reference store as an HGNC-symbol GMT and join directly to the symbol-keyed count matrix with no ID mapping. GO BP is present and used only as secondary, exploratory annotation of the hallmark hits.

Only 12,000 of ~20,000 human genes are present, so hallmark coverage is partial and must be reported per set rather than treating absent members as unchanged. n=6 per group with no batch structure supports a straightforward Wald test but not sub-group or interaction claims, and nothing here attempts them.
